title.purpose: The conversation header and a notice heading. The system ceiling at 18px.

body.purpose: Answers, messages, navigation rows, and controls. Prose is capped near 68 characters per line.

label.purpose: Buttons and the brand mark, at 14px and medium weight.

mono.purpose: Machine facts only: the interpretation readout, counts, card stats, identifiers.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The only filled control in the app. Normally one per screen, for the one action that matters.

components.name: Primary Action (link)

components.description: The server's own message, verbatim, beside the control that failed. The only non-amber color, and text only.

components.name: Card Tile
components.description: One card an answer was built from: its printed face in a rail-bordered frame at the card's own ratio, its name under it, the whole tile a link to the source the facts came from. A tile whose image will not load keeps the frame and the name, with a quiet note in the frame. A card the conversation's language has no printing of still appears, saying which language it is in under its name as text of its own rather than as part of the link, so the card is still announced by its name and the note is read after it.
components.html: Blue-Eyes White DragonEN only
components.css: .ds-card-tile { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 4px; } .ds-card { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 8px; text-decoration: none; } .ds-card:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid oklch(87.9% 0.169 91.605); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-card-frame { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; aspect-ratio: 421 / 614; border: 1px solid oklch(26.9% 0 none); background: oklch(20.5% 0 none); } .ds-card:hover .ds-card-frame { border-color: oklch(76.9% 0.188 70.08); } .ds-card-image { width: 100%; height: 100%; object-fit: contain; } .ds-card-name { color: oklch(97% 0 none); font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", Roboto, "Noto Sans", Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; line-height: 20px; } .ds-card-language { color: oklch(55.6% 0 none); font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Monaco, Consolas, "Liberation Mono", "Courier New", monospace; font-size: 12px; line-height: 16px; } .ds-card-missing { color: oklch(55.6% 0 none); font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", Roboto, "Noto Sans", Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; line-height: 20px; padding: 0 8px; text-align: center; }

components.name: Composer
components.description: Where the player asks for cards: what the last search was understood as above the field, a field on a 25% amber hairline, Send as the filled lamp of this surface carrying the arrow, and a live status line beside it. Opening a conversation puts the keyboard in the field. A turn that gave way is an alert line above the field.
components.css: .ds-composer { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 12px; border-top: 1px solid oklch(26.9% 0 none); padding: 24px; background: oklch(14.5% 0 none); } .ds-composer-field { width: 100%; resize: none; border: 1px solid oklch(76.9% 0.188 70.08 / 0.25); border-radius: 4px; background: oklch(20.5% 0 none); color: oklch(97% 0 none); padding: 8px 12px; font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", Roboto, "Noto Sans", Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; line-height: 20px; } .ds-composer-field::placeholder { color: oklch(55.6% 0 none); } .ds-composer-field:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid oklch(87.9% 0.169 91.605); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-composer-field:disabled { opacity: 0.6; } .ds-composer-row { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; gap: 12px; } .ds-composer-status { margin: 0; color: oklch(70.8% 0 none); font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", Roboto, "Noto Sans", Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; line-height: 20px; } .ds-composer-send { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; background: oklch(76.9% 0.188 70.08); color: oklch(27.9% 0.077 45.635); border: 0; border-radius: 4px; padding: 6px 10px; font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", Roboto, "Noto Sans", Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; line-height: 20px; } .ds-composer-send:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid oklch(87.9% 0.169 91.605); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-composer-send:disabled { opacity: 0.6; } .ds-composer-alert { margin: 0; color: oklch(70.4% 0.191 22.216); font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", Roboto, "Noto Sans", Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; line-height: 20px; }

components.name: Search Readout
components.description: What the last search was understood as: one fact per filter above the request field, the field it constrains quiet and what it asks of that field beside it. Facts rather than containers, set apart by space and never by a pill, a tag, or a box, and each fact is the control that corrects it, because the player is the one who knows what they asked for. A search that carried no filters says only that, and a turn that could not understand the request says so and repeats the words it fell back on. It is not a second live region: the status line announces the turn, and this is what is left once it is over.
components.css: .ds-readout { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 4px 16px; margin: 0; padding: 0; list-style: none; font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Monaco, Consolas, "Liberation Mono", "Courier New", monospace; font-size: 12px; line-height: 16px; } .ds-chip { border: 0; background: none; padding: 0; border-radius: 4px; text-align: left; color: oklch(55.6% 0 none); font: inherit; } .ds-chip:hover { color: oklch(97% 0 none); } .ds-chip:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid oklch(87.9% 0.169 91.605); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-chip-ask { color: oklch(70.8% 0 none); } .ds-chip:hover .ds-chip-ask { color: oklch(97% 0 none); } .ds-readout-note { margin: 0; color: oklch(70.8% 0 none); font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Monaco, Consolas, "Liberation Mono", "Courier New", monospace; font-size: 12px; line-height: 16px; }

components.name: Chip Editor
components.description: One filter being said: the field it constrains, then the operator and the value it takes, gathered the way that field takes them, a fixed set where the domain has one and a number where the field is a stat, so nothing can be built that the search would refuse. Correcting fixes the field, because the field is the part the readout is sure of; adding offers the fields the search supports and gathers the next operator and value the way the field that was chosen takes them. One group rather than loose controls, because what they say together is a single filter, and the group is where the keyboard arrives. Save or Add is out of action while the value is empty or the filter would be refused, and Escape calls the whole thing off.
components.css: .ds-chip-editor { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: center; gap: 8px; font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Monaco, Consolas, "Liberation Mono", "Courier New", monospace; font-size: 12px; line-height: 16px; } .ds-chip-control { border: 1px solid oklch(76.9% 0.188 70.08 / 0.25); border-radius: 4px; background: oklch(20.5% 0 none); color: oklch(97% 0 none); padding: 4px 6px; font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", Roboto, "Noto Sans", Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; line-height: 20px; } .ds-chip-control:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid oklch(87.9% 0.169 91.605); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-chip-action { border: 0; background: none; border-radius: 4px; padding: 0 4px; color: oklch(70.8% 0 none); font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", Roboto, "Noto Sans", Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; line-height: 20px; } .ds-chip-action:hover { color: oklch(97% 0 none); } .ds-chip-action:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid oklch(87.9% 0.169 91.605); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-chip-action:disabled { opacity: 0.6; }

components.name: Nav Row Action
components.description: A conversation's own controls, renaming and deleting, drawn as marks rather than words so the list stays a list of conversations. components.description: The control that folds the conversation list away and brings it back, as a pair of marks: the panel with its contents going in, and the panel with them coming out. narrative.overview:
A workbench is a surface with the thing you are working on laid out on it, and one lamp above it. That is the whole system. The surfaces are dark, near-neutral, and stepped rather than shadowed; the cards are the objects on the bench and get the room; amber is the lamp, and it appears where something is being offered, chosen, or focused, and nowhere else. The voice is quiet precision: small type set tightly, machine facts in mono, hairlines instead of containers, and no ornament between the player and the cards.

The bench is a direction rather than a finished expression. The incumbent implementation carries the surfaces, the amber, the density, and the flatness; the conversation surface, which is where the bench actually shows, is being built. Its history, its grid of framed cards, and the readout of what a search was understood as are in place, and the amber rail around the active turn and the model's reading set as marginalia follow.

Flatness is deliberate and the system has no motion yet. Depth is tonal: three steps of near-black do the work shadows would do elsewhere, and the only transition in the app is a color change that happens instantly.
keyCharacteristics: Near-neutral, three-step dark surfaces with no shadows.
One accent, amber, reserved for action, selection, and focus.
Density as craft: 14px body text, 12px mono for machine facts, 4px radius.
Hairline dividers instead of boxes, cards, or shadows.
The platform's font stack; no webfonts, no imagery in the chrome.
Keyboard first: every control reachable, focus always visible.

rules.name: The One Lamp Rule
rules.body: Amber marks what is actionable, chosen, or focused, and nothing else. No amber headings, no amber decoration, no amber dividers. Its rarity is what makes it read as light.

rules.name: The No Second Accent Rule
rules.body: There is no secondary or tertiary color. Failure is the only exception, it is text only, and it never becomes a fill.

rules.name: The No Display Rule
rules.body: Nothing shouts. 18px is the ceiling, and there is no display or headline size to reach for. Hierarchy comes from color, space, and hairlines, not from scale.

dos: Do keep amber for the action, the open row, and the focus ring, and count the amber elements on a screen; more than two is usually one too many.
Do step surfaces by one token (Room Black, Bench Slate, Rail Grey) when something needs to come forward, and keep them square.
Do use 1px Rail Grey hairlines to separate, and cap prose at about 68 characters and notices at 28rem.
Do set machine facts (filters, counts, card stats, identifiers) in 12px mono, and everything a person reads in the platform stack.
Do give a new full-page surface its own Room Black background. The frame carries it today and the document body stays transparent.
Do keep every control reachable by keyboard with a visible 2px Halo Amber outline, and keep aria-current on the open conversation.

Do keep an icon at 16px on a 1.5px stroke, the color of the control it sits in, beside the word it belongs to, or named for what it acts on when it is the whole control. The set is hand-drawn, and it does not grow a second weight, a fill, or a second size.

Do keep the pointer's affordances the pointer's: a folded conversation's mark, the fold control, and the list itself are each reachable without hovering, so no name and no conversation is behind a hover.
donts: Don't introduce a second accent, a gradient, or a colored heading; the one exception is Signal Red as text about a failure.
Don't go above 18px anywhere. If something needs more weight, change its color, its space, or its hairline instead.
Don't add shadows, blur, or elevation effects. If a surface needs to communicate hierarchy, use a tonal step.
Don't add motion without deciding the motion question first; the system is instant today by design, not by accident.

Don't introduce a webfont, an icon font, or an icon as decoration. The set is hand-drawn, one stroke weight, and it marks controls only: the cards, the conversation, and the notices carry no icons at all.
Don't crop, round, tilt, or restyle a card image. The card is a record of a real object and keeps its printed proportions.
Don't use a box, a card container, or a nested rectangle where a hairline and a spacing step would do.
Don't put a filter in a pill, a tag, or a box. A filter is a mono fact set apart by space, and where it is a control it is the fact itself rather than a container drawn around it.
